EXP34-C ORACLE COVERAGE, PART B (strict-only keys), sel4: src/fastpath/fastpath.c. These 6 keys are in-scope EXP34-C findings that aurora-lint d21be1b3d reports only at the strict preset (run sqc-0.6.0-d21be1b3d-strict-*; strict sets first_site_only=false and reports every dereference site, not only the first) and that no label covers. Same standard and method as coverage-exp34c-2026-10-calibration and coverage-exp34c-2026-10-part-a-curl-hostap-mbedtls-mosquitto: the dereference is the violation site, judged at strict under EXP34-C/2026-10-07/presets; FP needs proof in the scanned source, a language guarantee, or an ISO C or POSIX library contract (those rows also cite P/facts); open caller sets for exported functions; a strippable assert, a noreturn attribute and an earlier dereference of the same pointer are not proof. A later site inherits an earlier site's FP only when that proof also dominates it with no reassignment between. One read-only research reader drafted each verdict at source in the pinned checkout; the adjudicator reviewed every draft (format and vocabulary, every nearby opposite-verdict label, a source re-read of a sample and of the questioned rows) before inclusion.

RESULT: 6 FP, 0 TP.

FP shapes: reply == NULL tests that route to slowpath() or vm_fault_slowpath(), whose bodies end in restore_user_context() leaving the kernel through the exception return (consistent with the FP labels at fastpath.c:193 and :859); the notification Waiting-state invariant kept by every writer of the notification state and queue (medium).
